title: The Endless Harvest
premise: Folklorist Paloma Zhou arrives in the dying village of Hollowmere to record a harvest song that locals will sing only once, never twice, and never to its end. When an excavation crew breaches a stone door sealed from the inside, the village's oldest bargain breaks: something beneath the fields begins collecting what it was promised generations ago. As neighbors vanish into the harvest and the song's verses start writing themselves in her notebooks, Paloma must decide whether loyalty to the found family she's built among the villagers matters more than the truth of what they've done. In the end, she learns the final verse — and sings it alone, giving herself as the last verse's price, so that the door can be sealed again from the inside with her on the wrong side of it.
about_author: Elodie Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in rural communities before turning to fiction. She writes horror about the things families agree not to say out loud.

chapters.title: The Song They Sing Once
chapters.summary: Paloma Zhou arrives in Hollowmere with recording equipment and professional skepticism; innkeeper Maren Hale lets her hear one verse of the harvest song but goes pale when asked for a second take. POV: Paloma. Beat: curiosity sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Rules of Hospitality
chapters.summary: Maren feeds her, warns her gently — don't ask twice, don't hum it back, don't write the words down after dark. Paloma notes the superstitions clinically in her journal. POV: Paloma. Beat: the warmth of welcome laced with unspoken fear.

chapters.title: The Excavation
chapters.summary: A county crew surveying the flooded quarry field strikes dressed stone; foreman Denny Okafor jokes about cellars while the villagers stop working and simply watch. POV: Denny. Beat: modern confidence meeting old silence.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: The crew uncovers a door whose bolts are thrown from within; Paloma photographs it and finds the mortar scored with fingernail grooves. That night every dog in Hollowmere faces the field and howls once, together. POV: Paloma. Beat: dread arriving through evidence, not belief.

chapters.title: What Maren Won't Say
chapters.summary: Paloma presses Maren over dishes; Maren only says her grandmother 'paid early' and leaves the room. Teenager Ivo Hale, Maren's grandson, is friendlier — and hungry for stories of outside. POV: Paloma. Beat: first threads of found family.

chapters.title: The First Verse, Complete
chapters.summary: Paloma coaxes the full first verse from elderly Tam Broadbelt, who insists on singing it facing away from her. Her recorder plays back four voices where he sang alone. POV: Paloma. Beat: rational explanation beginning to strain.

chapters.title: Denny's Dream
chapters.summary: Denny dreams of standing inside the sealed door, hearing knocking, and wakes with dirt under his fingernails. His crew starts calling in sick. POV: Denny. Beat: the excavation becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Field at Night
chapters.summary: Paloma hears the song drifting from the empty field and follows it; wheat stands in rows no farmer planted, all bowed toward the door. She runs when something answers her footsteps in kind. POV: Paloma. Beat: skepticism cracking.

chapters.title: Parish Records
chapters.summary: In the church archive, Paloma finds harvest tallies going back centuries — names struck through in matched pairs, always two per generation, always in famine years. The vicar asks her to stop reading aloud. POV: Paloma. Beat: the pattern emerges.

chapters.title: Ivo Sings Along
chapters.summary: Ivo, showing off, hums the second verse he half-remembers; by morning his voice has changed pitch and he can't remember his mother's face. Maren slaps him hard enough to draw blood and calls it medicine. POV: Ivo. Beat: the cost made intimate.

chapters.title: The Village Meeting
chapters.summary: Hollowmere votes in the church basement: fill the shaft, or open the door properly and 'settle accounts.' Old grudges surface — some families were exempted from the tally, and everyone knows which ones. POV: Paloma. Beat: community fracturing along buried lines.

chapters.title: The Door Opens
chapters.summary: Despite the vote to seal it, someone opens the door overnight; cold air smelling of ripe grain pours out, and the wheat rows stand upright for the first time. Denny's missing laborer is found standing at the threshold, smiling, unable to speak. POV: Denny. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Second Voices
chapters.summary: Paloma's playback recordings now contain harmonies in voices she recognizes — the mute laborer, a drowned girl from 1974. The dead are singing the song forward, verse by verse, and the village can hear them too. POV: Paloma. Beat: horror through documentation.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren admits her grandmother took a neighbor's place in the tally, doubling another family's debt; the Hales have been 'early payers' ever since. She begs Paloma to leave before the song needs her. POV: Maren. Beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Second Verse
chapters.summary: The whole village wakes having dreamed the second verse identically; children draw it in the dirt. Paloma transcribes it against her own rule and finds the notation keeps rearranging itself overnight. POV: Paloma. Beat: knowledge as contagion.

chapters.title: Denny Descends
chapters.summary: Denny goes down the shaft with rope and floodlights to prove there's nothing there. He finds a granary the size of a cathedral, full, though Hollowmere hasn't had a real harvest in decades. Something counts him — aloud. POV: Denny. Beat: awe curdling to terror.

chapters.title: Quarantine of the Faithful
chapters.summary: Villagers begin marking their doors with wheat sheaves to show they've 'already paid'; unmarked houses wake to find their pantries full of grain no one bought. The exempted families' doors are stripped bare. POV: Ivo. Beat: the village turns on itself.

chapters.title: Tam's Last Recording
chapters.summary: Tam sings the third verse for Paloma voluntarily, saying someone should hold it true, then walks into the field at dusk and doesn't return. His boots are found neatly paired at the field's edge. POV: Paloma. Beat: grief braided with complicity.

chapters.title: The Tally Board
chapters.summary: Inside the church, the old tally board has updated itself: new names in fresh ink, including Denny's crew, including Ivo, including — in different handwriting — Paloma Zhou. The vicar burns it; it reappears on his own front door. POV: Paloma. Beat: being written into the story.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Maren offers herself in Ivo's place if the others help hide him; the exempted Wren family refuses to share their protection, and their barn burns that night — by human hands. POV: Maren. Beat: loyalty and truth pulling apart.

chapters.title: What the Dead Want
chapters.summary: The mute laborer writes one word repeatedly: FINISH. Paloma realizes the entity isn't stealing — it's owed a completion, a final verse the village stopped singing two centuries ago and has been paying interest on since. POV: Paloma. Beat: reframing horror as debt.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Archive
chapters.summary: The dying vicar shows Paloma the suppressed page: the original fourth verse, cut from every hymnal, which names the singer. Whoever completes the song becomes its keeper — or its payment. He dies before explaining which. POV: Paloma. Beat: hope with a hook in it.

chapters.title: Ivo Taken
chapters.summary: Ivo vanishes from a locked room; wheat grows through the floorboards. Maren shatters. Paloma finds him in the field, walking the rows in step with dozens of others, all mouthing lyrics. He waves at her, smiling, still himself — barely. POV: Maren. Beat: heartbreak at the edge of the field.

chapters.title: The Crew Breaks
chapters.summary: Denny's remaining workers flee en route to blow the shaft closed; the explosives detonate harmlessly, packed grain-dust deadening everything. Denny realizes the ground won't let them leave — the county road now loops back to Hollowmere. POV: Denny. Beat: escape denied.

chapters.title: Singing Lessons
chapters.summary: Paloma studies the corrupted fourth verse with Maren, learning to sing it without 'singing along' — holding the melody while refusing the meaning. It works for exactly eight bars. The ninth bar sings itself in her voice. POV: Paloma. Beat: mastery and its limits.

chapters.title: The Wren Bargain
chapters.summary: The Wrens reveal their exemption: an ancestor sang the song to completion once, alone, and was spared — but the debt merely transferred to the village entire. Their protection is expiring tonight. POV: Paloma. Beat: the precedent, and its terrible fine print.

chapters.title: Night of the Full Pantries
chapters.summary: Every house fills with grain; the starving village could eat for a year if they dare touch it. Some do, and wake up humming harmonies. Hunger versus faith splits families at their own tables. POV: Ivo (from the field). Beat: temptation as siege warfare.

chapters.title: Rescue Party
chapters.summary: Maren and Denny walk into the field for Ivo, following Paloma's map of safe intervals between verses. They reach him; he refuses to leave — 'the rows are warm, Mum, and nobody's lonely here.' They carry him out anyway, screaming. POV: Maren. Beat: love against consent.

chapters.title: The Price of Carrying Him
chapters.summary: Pulling Ivo free costs the party: Denny's left hand comes back aged forty years, and Maren can no longer speak above a whisper — her voice partially kept below. The tally board adds a column. POV: Denny. Beat: rescue has receipts.

chapters.title: Verse Four, Found
chapters.summary: Paloma pieces the complete fourth verse from Tam's recording, the vicar's page, and the dead girl's harmony on her tapes. Its final line requires a name freely given. She understands what 'finishing' means. POV: Paloma. Beat: the trap fully visible.

chapters.title: Everyone's Plan
chapters.summary: The village convenes its last honest meeting: draw lots, force the Wrens, or let Paloma sing. Each option is monstrous. Maren quietly volunteers; Paloma refuses to let her, and lies about why. POV: Paloma. Beat: loyalty weaponized both ways.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: The night stretches; dawn doesn't come. Clocks run backward in the church. The field walks closer to the houses row by row, patient as arithmetic. Villagers hold each other and sing the first three verses loudly, wrongly, defiantly. POV: Ivo. Beat: communal courage as stalling action.

chapters.title: Maren's Attempt
chapters.summary: Maren steals down to the door at false-dawn and begins the fourth verse in her ruined whisper; the song rejects her incomplete voice, and the backlash takes her memory of Ivo entirely. Paloma drags her back. POV: Maren. Beat: sacrifice refused by the machinery of debt.

chapters.title: The Truth About the Exemption
chapters.summary: Paloma deciphers the Wren ancestor's diary: she didn't finish the song — she started a new one, resetting the debt onto everyone else. There is no clean ending, only choosing who carries it. Paloma chooses. POV: Paloma. Beat: agency seized from a rigged game.

chapters.title: Goodbyes
chapters.summary: Paloma spends the frozen evening teaching Ivo her folklore methods, recording Maren's memories of her, leaving instructions and letters. She asks Denny to make sure the recordings survive and the truth gets told — even the ugly parts. POV: Paloma. Beat: farewell without melodrama.

chapters.title: The Fifth Verse
chapters.summary: At the door, Paloma discovers there was always a fifth verse — unwritten because it belongs to whoever sings fourth. She begins, and the song offers her everything: Ivo whole, Maren's voice, endless harvests, forever. POV: Paloma. Beat: temptation at maximum power.

chapters.title: Freely Given
chapters.summary: She declines the gifts, names herself plainly, and sings the fifth verse as composition rather than capitulation — changing the terms instead of paying them. The door accepts a keeper, not a meal. The wheat bows once, all together, like a congregation. POV: Paloma. Beat: triumph through refusal.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: The door closes with Paloma's hands on the bolts — thrown from within, as they always were. The field goes fallow. Ivo wakes remembering everything, which is its own wound. Maren finds Paloma's recorder on the threshold, still running. POV: Maren. Beat: victory shaped like loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Spring comes late but real. Denny delivers the tapes to an archive; the county lists the site as collapsed. Hollowmere plants a crop it intends to eat. Ivo takes up the folklore work, recording honestly, asking nothing twice. POV: Ivo. Beat: grief metabolized into vocation.

chapters.title: Coda: One Verse, Twice
chapters.summary: Years later, Ivo visits the sealed door with his own students and sings the first verse — then, deliberately, sings it again. Nothing happens. Or almost nothing: faintly, warmly, from the other side, someone hums the harmony. POV: Ivo. Beat: ambiguous grace note ending.
